partners.diseaseBName: facial palsy, congenital, with ptosis and velopharyngeal dysfunction
partners.mechanism_chain: GJA5 (HGNC:4194) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac conduction (GO:0007578); Cardiac conduction (GO:0007578) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial standstill (HP:0005161); TUBB6 (HGNC:27114) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal development (GO:0048666); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital facial palsy (HP:0001348); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Ptosis (HP:0000521); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Velopharyngeal dysfunction (HP:0001640). Haploinsufficiency of GJA5 disrupts cardiac conduction, leading to atrial standstill. Concurrently, haploinsufficiency of TUBB6 disrupts neuronal development, contributing to congenital facial palsy, ptosis, and velopharyngeal dysfunction. The shared mechanism lies in the distinct but critical roles of these genes within their respective cellular modules, suggesting a broader implication of gene dosage in complex developmental processes.

partners.mechanism_chain: GJA5 (HGNC:4102) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885); GJC2 (HGNC:24942) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885); Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial standstill (HP:0005175); Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885) —LEADS_TO→ Spastic paraplegia (HP:0002060). #### 1. facial palsy, congenital, with ptosis and velopharyngeal dysfunction  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-190861)

**Proposed mechanism:** GJA5 (HGNC:4194) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac conduction (GO:0007578); Cardiac conduction (GO:0007578) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial standstill (HP:0005161); TUBB6 (HGNC:27114) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal development (GO:0048666); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital facial palsy (HP:0001348); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Ptosis (HP:0000521); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Velopharyngeal dysfunction (HP:0001640). Haploinsufficiency of GJA5 disrupts cardiac conduction, leading to atrial standstill. Concurrently, haploinsufficiency of TUBB6 disrupts neuronal development, contributing to congenital facial palsy, ptosis, and velopharyngeal dysfunction. The shared mechanism lies in the distinct but critical roles of these genes within their respective cellular modules, suggesting a broader implication of gene dosage in complex developmental processes.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of individuals with heterozygous loss-of-function variants in GJA5 who do not exhibit atrial standstill, or individuals with heterozygous loss-of-function variants in TUBB6 who do not exhibit congenital facial palsy, ptosis, or velopharyngeal dysfunction. _(variant: The presence of common variants (MAF > 1%) in the coding regions of GJA5 or TUBB6 in the general population that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared principle of gene dosage sensitivity in distinct developmental modules (cardiac and neuronal) could inform therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating gene expression or function in related conditions. Targeting pathways downstream of GJA5 or TUBB6 may offer novel treatment avenues for both atrial standstill and congenital facial palsy syndromes.

#### 2. hereditary spastic paraplegia 44  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.379)

**Proposed mechanism:** GJA5 (HGNC:4102) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885); GJC2 (HGNC:24942) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885); Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial standstill (HP:0005175); Gap junction complex assembly and function (GO:0005885) —LEADS_TO→ Spastic paraplegia (HP:0002060). Mutations in GJA5 lead to atrial standstill by disrupting the assembly and function of gap junctions in the heart. Similarly, mutations in GJC2 disrupt gap junction function in neurons, leading to hereditary spastic paraplegia. Both disease mechanisms converge on the impairment of the gap junction complex, a shared pathway essential for normal cardiac and neuronal function.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in GJA5 or GJC2 with a minor allele frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD, or demonstration of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways affected by mutations in each gene. _(variant: GJA5 or GJC2 pathogenic variants)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of gap junctions in cardiac and neurological function can inform therapeutic strategies that target intercellular communication for a range of disorders. Modulating gap junction function could potentially alleviate symptoms in both atrial standstill and hereditary spastic paraplegia.
